answer_1.quote: Transformer-based language models (LMs) trained on web-scale corpora are generating impressively realistic texts... sampling text from LMs to satisfy constraints on the properties of generated text
datasets: Jigsaw Unintended Bias In Toxicity Classification Kaggle Challenge
answer_1.outputs: The paper evaluates generated outputs across multiple NLG tasks including translation, summarization, dialog, and prompt completion, with constraints on toxicity, sentiment, keywords, and entities.

answer_2.quote: We evaluate the generated samples along three dimension, (1) Constraint Satisfaction measured using external evaluators, (2) Fluency, measured by mean perplexity of the continuations measured using GPT2-XL... (3) Diversity, measured by computing the mean number of distinct n-grams in each set of samples, normalized by the length of text

answer_4.quote: we also perform human evaluation in an A/B testing setup with the best performing baseline (DExperts in our case). For each sample, we ask 3 annotators to compare and rank candidates from our approach and the baseline on constraint satisfaction, topicality and fluency
answer_4.guideline: Annotators are asked to compare and rank outputs from two methods on constraint satisfaction, topicality, and fluency in an A/B testing setup.
